If D is zero, there is one real solution, x = -b / (2a). If D is negative, there are no real solutions.

To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first find the derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions to this equation are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine whether each stationary point is a maximum, minimum, or saddle point, find the second derivative of the function, f''(x), and evaluate it at each stationary point. If f''(x) is positive, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) is negative, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) is zero, the point is a saddle point.
